topics.title: Habitats and their biotic and abiotic components

concepts.learning_objective: Define a habitat and recognise that habitats can be large or very small.
Distinguish the biotic and abiotic components of a habitat and the needs each meets.
Explain how different organisms coexist in one habitat by using it in different ways.

topics.title: Populations, communities and the role of every organism

concepts.learning_objective: Define a population as a group of the same kind of organisms in a habitat at a given time.
Describe a community as different populations sharing the same habitat.
Interpret how fish in a pond indirectly affect seed production in nearby plants.

topics.title: Interactions in an ecosystem; producers and consumers

concepts.learning_objective: Classify interactions as biotic-abiotic, abiotic-abiotic or among biotic components.
Define an ecosystem and identify aquatic, terrestrial and human-made ecosystems.
Classify organisms as autotrophs or heterotrophs, and consumers as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores.

topics.title: Food chains, trophic levels and food webs

concepts.learning_objective: Represent and interpret who eats whom as a linear food chain.
Identify the trophic level occupied by an organism in a food chain.
Explain how interlinked food chains form a food web.
Identify decomposers (saprotrophs) such as fungi and bacteria and what they do.
Explain how decomposition returns nutrients to the soil so that nothing in nature is wasted.

topics.title: Changes, balance and relationships in ecosystems

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how one change in an ecosystem leads to a chain of further changes.
Explain how competition for resources controls population size and keeps an ecosystem balanced.
Distinguish mutualism, commensalism and parasitism with examples.

topics.title: Benefits of ecosystems, threats and human-made ecosystems

concepts.learning_objective: List the benefits humans obtain from forest and aquatic ecosystems.
Identify human threats to ecosystems such as the Sundarbans and the role of protected areas.
Describe human-made ecosystems and why they need human care and management.
Describe the Green Revolution and why its methods are now considered unsustainable.
Explain how overuse of synthetic chemicals and monoculture harm soil, pollinators and pest control.
Identify organic and traditional practices that support sustainable farming.
